core_obligations: Identify the displayed complex with the complex associated to the cosimplicial object obtained by iterating the adjoint pair f_*f^*, and note that the augmentation F to f_*f^*F is the natural map (proof lines 7041-7047).

Show every term is flasque: pushforward from the discrete space X is flasque because a pushforward of a flasque sheaf is flasque, so each f_*f^*...f_*f^*F is a flasque O_X-module (proof lines 7048-7051).

Prove the stalkwise homotopy equivalence: since (f^*G)_x = G_x the functor f^* is exact, exactness may be tested after pulling back, and the cosimplicial homotopy result from the introduction to the section gives the homotopy equivalence at every stalk (proof lines 7054-7078).
proof_roadmap: Recognise the complex as a cosimplicial construction (proof lines 7041-7047).
Establish flasqueness of the terms (proof lines 7048-7051).
Reduce the homotopy statement to the cosimplicial homotopy result after pulling back (proof lines 7054-7078).
difficulty_reason: For a ringed space (X, O_X) and a sheaf of O_X-modules F, the lemma produces a functorial resolution 0 to F to f_*f^*F to f_*f^*f_*f^*F to ..., each term flasque, such that at every point x the induced map F_x[0] to the complex of stalks is a homotopy equivalence of complexes of O_{X,x}-modules (statement lines 7014-7038). The proof identifies the complex as the one associated to a cosimplicial object built from the adjoint pair f^* and f_*, observes that pushforward from the discrete space is flasque because a pushforward of a flasque sheaf is flasque, and then argues stalkwise: since (f^*G)_x = G_x the functor f^* is exact, so exactness and homotopy can be tested after pulling back, which lets the author invoke the cosimplicial homotopy result stated in the introduction to the section (proof lines 7040-7078). The claim is H2: standard inputs, with the identification of the complex as the one attached to a cosimplicial object and the stalkwise reduction as the parts that must be followed.
